behavioral disturbances are related to the supero- and infra-medial prefrontal areas.

the study of the neuroanatomical basis for the behavioral and cognitive disturbances in patients with frontal lesions.

the prefrontal areas involved in the behavioral disturbances are those areas involved in the control of behavior, and that these areas are not necessarily the same areas involved in the cognitive deficits.

behavioral disturbances in patients after frontal lesions can be explained as the result of the loss of a specific prefrontal system.
prefrontal patients show a global impairment in their cognitive abilities and, at the same time, a specific impairment in the behavioral control of their actions.
the prefrontal lobe is involved in the control of behavior and cognition.

the behavioral disturbances in prefrontal cortex patients are related to the neuroanatomical characteristics of the lesion.
behavioral disturbances are more closely related to the anatomical integrity of the frontal cortex than to cognitive abilities.
